synopsis: Chapter 12 identifies the IDEA protocol (Hemming and colleagues, 2018), alongside SHELF and EFSA guidance, as a practical procedure for structured elicitation of quantities [f9947]. The glossary describes IDEA, Cooke’s Classical Model and SHELF as protocols for numerical judgments, such as durations and error magnitudes, that calibrate experts against questions with known answers [f16363]. The planning recommendation puts IDEA-style elicitation of durations and probabilities in month 2 of the preparation sequence [f9971]. The supplied facts do not specify the calibration questions or implementation details for that month-2 exercise [f16363, f9971].

relations.note: Adds numerical judgment examples and calibration against questions with known answers.
Turns the general elicitation method into a month-2 planning recommendation.
Suitability for numerical judgments supports using IDEA to elicit durations and probabilities.
